verdict.rationale: Pipedream's docs show built-in failure notification: by default it emails when a workflow throws an unhandled error, surfaces error details and stack traces, and supports automatic retries for errored events. The evidence never shows a dedicated error-handling path or separate error workflow that an ops user can define, so only the notification half of the story is delivered. Missing for 10: documented dedicated error-handling branches or error workflows, configurable notification channels beyond email, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can define dedicated error-handling paths or error workflows and get notified when a run fails

citations.quote: By default, Pipedream sends an email when a workflow throws an unhandled error.
You can automatically retry events that yield an error. This can help for transient errors that occur when making API requests, like when a service is down or your request times out.
Pipedream will surface details about the error and the stack trace, and you can even debug these errors with AI.
